newsitem.title: USA: CHRYSLER SETS 1998 PRICES LOWER BY 0.6 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: CHRYSLER SETS 1998 PRICES LOWER BY 0.6 PERCENT.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. followed its competitors Wednesday in holding the line on the prices of its 1998 cars and trucks.
Chrysler, the No. 3 U.S. automaker, said the average price of its 1998 models will be 0.6 percent lower than the price of comparably equipped 1997 models.

"This pricing reflects the realities of a competitive marketplace, but more important, it represents Chrysler's continuing success at cutting costs and finding efficiencies ..." said James Holden, executive vice president - sales and marketing, in a news release.
Holden said some prices will be lower and others will be higher, but the average will be 0.6 percent lower than a year ago.
As an example, Chrysler said a typically equipped four-door Dodge and Plymouth Neon "Highline" will have a suggested retail price of $13,455, down from $13,770.

On a sales weighted average, suggested prices for 1998 passenger cars will be 1.3 percent lower than prices on comparably equipped 1997 models. Prices on trucks, including minivans and Jeep vehicles, reflect an average decline of 0.4 percent.
The prices do not include vehicles that will be launched later this year, such as the 1998 Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde, Dodge Durango, and Dodge Ram Van and Wagon.

Earlier this week, Ford Motor Co. said prices on its 1998 models will be unchanged from 1997 models and General Motors Corp. said its prices would increase by 1.3 percent, its smallest price rise in more than a decade.
